text:
Jeanne's Cupboard, the on-campus food pantry at UMass Dartmouth, has become an essential resource for 
students, faculty, staff, and community members experiencing food insecurity. Nationally, nearly 3 in 5 college 
students experience some form of basic needs insecurity, while 38% of students attending Massachusetts public 
universities are food insecure. At UMass Dartmouth, a recent student survey found that more than one-third of 
respondents experienced food insecurity while enrolled, underscoring the growing need for campus-based support. 
The pantry's continued success is made possible through the collaborative efforts of the University, dedicated 
student employees and volunteers, generous donors, and valued partners such as the Greater Boston Food Bank 
(GBFB), the Massachusetts Department of Higher Education's Hunger Free Campus Initiative, and benefactors 
Jeanne and Bob Leduc. In addition to providing food, GBFB gift cards enable Jeanne's Cupboard to purchase 
hygiene products and other essential household items, helping address the broader issue of basic needs insecurity. 
As demand has continued to increase, Jeanne's Cupboard has expanded significantly. During 2025-2026, the 
pantry's monthly food allocation from the Greater Boston Food Bank has grown to approximately 5,000 pounds of 
food each month, allowing the pantry to distribute 49,312 pounds of food during the academic year, the equivalent 
of more than 41,000 meals. During that same period, the pantry recorded 7,125 pantry visits, demonstrating both the 
growing demand for services and the vital role the pantry plays in supporting the community. 
Food insecurity is more than a matter of hunger, it directly affects students' academic success, physical and mental 
health, and their ability to remain enrolled. Jeanne's Cupboard represents far more than emergency food assistance, 
it is an investment in student success, equity, and well-being. Through the dedication of student employees, 
volunteers, university leadership, community partners, and generous donors, the pantry has created a welcoming, 
stigma-free environment where every member of the campus community is treated with dignity and compassion.
